children.topic: Choledocholithiasis (CBD Stones)
Origin: Secondary (passed from gallbladder via cystic duct - 85-90%) vs Primary (formed in duct due to stasis/infection - 10-15%)
Clinical Presentation: Biliary colic, obstructive jaundice (dark urine, pale stools, pruritus), fluctuating jaundice
Lab Findings: Cholestatic LFT pattern (↑↑ ALP, ↑↑ GGT, ↑ Direct Bilirubin, mild ALT/AST rise)
Courvoisier Law: In presence of obstructive jaundice, a palpable non-tender GB is unlikely due to gallstones (more likely pancreatic head / biliary malignancy)
Risk Stratification (ASGE Guidelines)
High Risk (>50%): Stone on US, Ascending cholangitis, Total Bilirubin >4 mg/dL + dilated CBD (>6mm)
Management: Direct ERCP + Sphincterotomy + Stone extraction
Intermediate Risk (10-50%): Abnormal LFTs, Dilated CBD (>6mm) on US, Age >50
Management: EUS or MRCP (or Intraoperative Cholangiogram - IOC)
Low Risk (<10%): Normal LFTs, normal CBD diameter, no stone seen
Management: Proceed directly to Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy without pre-op ERCP
Acute Cholangitis
Pathophysiology: Biliary stasis + bacterial infection → elevated intrabiliary pressure (>25 cmH₂O) → transcholangitic translocation of bacteria into blood
Charcot's Triad (70% of cases): 1. RUQ abdominal pain 2. Jaundice 3. Fever with chills/rigors
Reynolds' Pentad (Severe / Suppurative Cholangitis): Charcot's Triad + 4. Hypotension (septic shock) 5. Altered mental status
Tokyo Guidelines (TG18) for Cholangitis: Diagnostic criteria (A. Systemic inflammation B. Cholestasis C. Biliary imaging evidence)
Management of Cholangitis & CBD Stones
Initial Resuscitation: IV fluids, NPO, blood cultures, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (Piperacillin-Tazobactam or Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole)
Biliary Decompression (Cornerstone of Therapy):
Emergency ERCP + Sphincterotomy + Biliary Stent / Stone Removal (<12-24 hours for severe, <48h for mild/moderate)
PTBD (Percutaneous Transhepatic Biliary Drainage) if ERCP fails or altered anatomy (Roux-en-Y)
Surgical CBD Exploration (Choledochotomy + T-tube placement) if endoscopic/radiologic intervention unavailable
Definitive Treatment: Interval Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy after cholangitis settles to prevent recurrent gallstone complications
